prompt: Name an English word borrowed from Japanese

answers.name: Sushi
answers.fact: Originally fish preserved in fermented rice.

answers.name: Emoji
answers.fact: 'Picture character'. Its likeness to 'emotion' is a coincidence.

answers.name: Anime
answers.fact: A Japanese shortening of the English word 'animation'.

answers.name: Ninja
answers.fact: Written with characters about enduring and concealing.

answers.name: Tycoon
answers.fact: From 'taikun', 'great lord', a title used for the shogun.

answers.name: Honcho
answers.fact: From 'hanchō', squad leader; US soldiers brought it home.

answers.name: Sake
answers.fact: In Japan, 'sake' means any alcohol; the rice wine is often called nihonshu.

answers.name: Ramen
answers.fact: Japan's spin on Chinese noodle soup.

answers.name: Tofu
answers.fact: Came to Japan from China; English got the word via Japanese.

answers.name: Wasabi
answers.fact: Most 'wasabi' outside Japan is dyed horseradish.

answers.name: Tempura
answers.fact: Probably from a word used by Portuguese missionaries.

answers.name: Futon
answers.fact: In Japan, a thin mattress folded away each morning.

answers.name: Kamikaze
answers.fact: 'Divine wind', after typhoons that wrecked Mongol fleets.

answers.name: Umami
answers.fact: The fifth taste, named by chemist Kikunae Ikeda in 1908.

answers.name: Bento
answers.fact: A packed lunch in a box.

answers.name: Reiki
answers.fact: A healing practice developed in 1920s Japan.

answers.name: Shiitake
answers.fact: 'Shii' is the tree it grows on; 'take' means mushroom.

answers.name: Panko
answers.fact: Japanese breadcrumbs; 'pan' comes from the Portuguese for bread.

answers.name: Tsundoku
answers.fact: Buying books and letting them pile up unread.

answers.name: Kaizen
answers.fact: Continuous improvement, made famous by Toyota.

answers.name: Kendo
answers.fact: 'Way of the sword', fought with bamboo swords.

answers.name: Tatami
answers.fact: Floor mats; Japanese rooms are still measured in them.

answers.name: Torii
answers.fact: The gateway to a Shinto shrine.

answers.name: Nunchaku
answers.fact: From Okinawa, made famous by Bruce Lee.

answers.name: Netsuke
answers.fact: Tiny carved toggles for hanging things from a kimono sash.

answers.name: Skosh
answers.fact: US slang for 'a little bit', from 'sukoshi', picked up by soldiers.

answers.name: Kudzu
answers.fact: A Japanese vine that has run wild across the US South.

answers.name: Satsuma
answers.fact: The mandarin is named after a former province of Japan.
